name: Rasuwa (Nepal–Tibet border) outburst flood
summary: Ice–rock avalanche high on the Nepal–Tibet border sent a flash flood of water, ice, rock and mud through valleys in Rasuwa district (Nepal) and adjacent Tibet. The collapse produced a seismic signal initially catalogued by USGS as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake and later reinterpreted as the avalanche itself.

mechanism.value: ice-rock avalanche; cascading river damming and outburst reported
mechanism.source: press synthesis (Geology Page; severe-weather.eu citing USGS; Science Times), 2026-08-27

initial_catalog_magnitude.source: press reports citing USGS initial catalog entry
initial_catalog_magnitude.note: Initially reported as a tectonic earthquake; later attributed to the avalanche mass movement itself. Whether this signature is separable from ordinary seismicity fast enough to warn downstream is issue #1 — the question this project exists to get answered.

deaths_reported.source: Associated Press via CNN live coverage, late 2026-08-26
deaths_reported.note: Press-derived inside 72 hours of the event, spanning Nepal and China combined. Presumed wrong in detail; re-verify against NDRRMA (Nepal) and official Chinese tallies.

missing_reported.source: press reports say 'hundreds' — no figure stable enough to record
missing_reported.note: Record a number only when an official tally exists.

infrastructure.value: roads, bridges, settlements and hydropower installations reported swept away or buried; border access reported extremely difficult

source_to_first_settlement_km.note: Filled by the corridor inventory (weeks 3–4) from mapped geometry, not estimated.

flood_wave_travel_time_min.note: Determines whether any warning is usable. Requires hydraulic input; never guessed.
